q: Does rice husk fuel lower a Vietnamese cement kiln's CBAM figure?
title: Rice husk in cement kilns and CBAM
short: It can, if the husk qualifies as biomass under the CBAM rules, which refer to EU sustainability criteria. Qualifying biomass CO2 is counted at zero, and only the fossil share of the fuel mix stays. Keep purchase records, calorific values and the evidence that the husk is a residue.
audience: Cement plants in Vietnam's Mekong and northern provinces replacing coal with rice husk or other agricultural residues

ul: Tonnes of husk fired, with moisture and calorific value.
Supplier invoices showing it is a processing residue.
The coal or petcoke it replaced, for your own trend.

p: Calcination CO2 from limestone does not change with fuel, and it is usually the larger part of clinker emissions. Rice husk ash also adds silica to the kiln feed, so watch clinker chemistry.
